$comment: Rule catalog — line movement, staleness, closing-line value. Standards 15, 16, 17.

rules.title: Line movement is recorded where it is available
rules.description: Where the book publishes earlier prices, the decision records them with their timestamps.
rules.rationale: How a price moved before a decision is information about what the market learned. It is recommended rather than required because not every book publishes a history, and a rule that required one would push a bettor toward inventing it.
rules.remediation: Record the observed prices with their capture times.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance over what was recorded. Absence of a line history is not distinguishable from a book that publishes none, which is why this rule is recommended.

rules.title: Price and prediction freshness are checked before deciding
rules.description: Every decision records when the price was captured and when the prediction was made, and no BET rests on either beyond the policy's age limits or after the event has started.
rules.rationale: A stale input with an apparent edge is the most dangerous kind, because the number looks like evidence and is not: the price may no longer be offered, and the prediction may describe a world that has since changed.
rules.remediation: Re-capture the price, re-run the prediction, or record a PASS.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance from timestamp arithmetic over recorded values. It establishes that the recorded capture time is within the window, not that the price was actually current at that time.

rules.title: Closing-line value is computed where the closing price is obtainable
rules.description: Where a closing price can be observed, settled records carry it and the resulting closing-line value. Where it cannot, its absence is recorded as absence and never estimated.
rules.rationale: Closing-line value is the best available evidence about process quality on a sample far smaller than profit and loss requires, because it measures whether the decision found a price the market later agreed with rather than whether the outcome went your way.
rules.remediation: Record the closing price and compute the value. If no closing price is available, leave the field absent rather than filling in an estimate.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full arithmetic assurance where a closing price is recorded; no assurance at all about records where it is absent, since an unobtainable close and an unrecorded one look identical.

rules.title: Line movement is never fabricated
rules.description: No price history, closing price, or claim about how a line moved is invented, back-filled from memory, or reconstructed after the fact.
rules.rationale: Fabricated movement corrupts the one metric that grades process rather than outcome. A record showing the line moved toward every position would make a losing process look skilled indefinitely, and it is the easiest number in the ledger to invent because nobody checks a price that no longer exists.
rules.remediation: Record only observed prices with their capture times. An unobserved price is recorded as absent.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects only structural impossibilities — a history whose timestamps or prices are inconsistent with the record around them. An invented but plausible price history passes this check entirely. It MUST NOT be reported as establishing that line movement is genuine.
